subtype: Approach: weekly burn review with a kill threshold [Revision]
passage: I share a co-working table with two founders, Reena and Jagdish, and every Friday at five they close their laptops and open a notebook. One column for what they spent that week, one for sign-ups. I have watched this for months. In March the sign-ups grew but nobody paid. Reena had written a number at the top of the page and circled it: if the runway dropped under four months and still nobody paid, they would cut. In April it did. The next Monday they cancelled the paid design tool, thanked the freelancer, and started phoning shop owners themselves, one by one, phone on speaker. I could not tell what they felt. Jagdish looked flat for a couple of days. But by Friday there was a new entry in the sign-ups column, with a small tick beside it.

qa.q: What did the founders cut when cash fell below four months?
qa.a: They cancelled the paid design tool and thanked the freelancer.

qa.q: What might Jagdish have felt after the cuts, according to the narrator?
qa.a: The narrator cannot tell for sure, but Jagdish looked flat for a couple of days, so may have felt disappointed.

qa.q: What else could the founders do besides selling personally?
qa.a: They could ask the sign-ups why nobody pays, and adjust what they offer based on the answers.

qa.q: How does the narrator see the weekly review?
qa.a: The narrator sees it as disciplined, since the limit was set in advance and the decision was not made in panic.

grounding: The founders compare spending with sign-ups each Friday and, when cash falls below the set threshold with no paying user, cut costs and sell personally.
